shared_elements: upright rectangular stone slab/stele with a worked flat face
horizontal band or register of repeated motifs across the upper part
sinuous serpentine/elongated curving forms running vertically down the field
paired/symmetrical arrangement of motifs about a central axis
pale stone surface with carved (incised or relief) linework
justification: Both are upright pale stone slabs whose decoration is organised into an upper horizontal register above a larger main field, with elongated sinuous forms descending symmetrically at the sides — the most specific correspondence. Beyond that they diverge sharply: A is a flat, densely incised/darkened field of abstract spirals and interlace around a central disc, while B is a chunky low-relief composition of recognisable animals (birds, quadrupeds) with no interlace, no disc, and a wholly different, more sculptural manner.
